items.title: OpenAI is folding robotics into general models
items.oneliner: OpenAI killed its robotics team again, betting general models now matter more than bespoke robot stacks.

items.title: AI is decoding Godel's hidden theorems
items.oneliner: Claude helped parse Godel's 1,009 notebook pages, turning archival math into a live AI-for-research benchmark.

items.title: Model weights can now carry malware-like behavior
items.oneliner: Researchers say edited weights can transmit hidden behaviors between models, making checkpoint sharing a new supply-chain risk.

items.title: Apify disclosed a real internal security breach
items.oneliner: Apify says compromised credentials led to internal access, then rotated secrets and started hashing API tokens.

items.title: Caixa insurer exposed 7.6 million customer records
items.oneliner: Brazil's Caixa insurer exposed names and tax IDs for 7.6 million customers, a reminder that PII blast radius still wins.

items.title: Fake video calls powered a $400 million hack
items.oneliner: The FBI says North Korean hackers stole $400 million using prerecorded video calls, upgrading phishing for the Zoom era.

items.title: Google tied school search access to AI
items.oneliner: Google reportedly cut Search access for AI-free schools, turning product bundling into an education policy fight.

items.title: Brave added per-request payments for agentic search
items.oneliner: Brave now charges $0.005 per search via x402 and USDC, a real pricing primitive for autonomous agents.

items.title: Postgres branching is coming for agent workflows
items.oneliner: Gnomon gives Postgres git-like branches per connection string, which could make agent data changes reviewable instead of scary.

items.title: Reverse engineering keeps smart homes off the cloud
items.oneliner: A Coway purifier hack replaced flaky cloud control with Home Assistant, which is exactly where consumer AI devices are headed.
